title: Add task: Tighten a tourniquet's windlass to the green and lock it by CHANCHIPUI · Pull Request #1026 · robocurve/benchmark-tasks · GitHub
comments: Adds tasks/tourniquet-windlass/ (Societal relevance). The instruction is "Tighten the tourniquet on the training leg until its gauge reads green, then lock the rod in its clip." A training thigh lies across the table with a windlass tourniquet strapped round it. A pressure gauge on the band's bladder reads 60 mmHg; its dial is green from 250. The robot has to: turn the windlass rod, which tightens the band and raises the gauge; keep hold of it, since the band turns it back the moment nothing holds or locks it; regrip as it goes: a gripper turns it at most about 200 degrees in one hold, and it needs 210, so something has to hold the rod meanwhile (the other hand in the demo, or the clip); lock it only in the green: the clip lines up every half turn, first 30 degrees in with the gauge at about 90; push the rod's end down past the clip's lips and let go. Scoring, from a photo of the gauge and the clip and the video: 1.0: gauge at 250 or more, the rod locked, and no part of the robot within 1 cm of the rod or clip for the last 1 s; 0.5: in the green but the rod still held, or locked with the robot still within 1 cm; 0.25: locked with the gauge under 250; 0 otherwise, including letting go unlocked. Media: M-YS4ANC (Dream-1 run, demo, setup screenshot). Both videos show all three cameras: top, left arm and right arm. Scores: Dream-1 run 0.0 (it pushed the rod round 9 degrees once but never locked it); scripted demo 1.0 (553 steps). The demo regrips once with the other hand holding the rod, and checks the gauge on its needle before locking. Scripted variants: locking at the first chance scores 0.25, holding in the green without locking 0.5, letting go to regrip with nothing holding the rod 0, and keeping a hand on after locking 0.5. The let-go check uses yam_arena's collision hulls of every link, the gripper body and both fingers. The clip's lips are not modelled; once the rod is 7 mm in, task code holds it down as they would (stated in fidelity). Run and demo commands, scoring details, the real-world build with its calibration, and simulation fidelity are in the task's README.md.
